```kotlin
package com.discountscreener.android.ui.dashboard

import androidx.compose.foundation.background
import androidx.compose.foundation.clickable
import androidx.compose.foundation.isSystemInDarkTheme
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.padding
import androidx.compose.foundation.shape.RoundedCornerShape
import androidx.compose.material3.MaterialTheme
import androidx.compose.material3.Text
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.draw.clip
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color
import androidx.compose.ui.text.font.FontWeight
import androidx.compose.ui.text.style.TextOverflow
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import com.discountscreener.android.presentation.dashboard.QuantLensChipUi
import com.discountscreener.android.presentation.dashboard.QuantLensQualifier

/**
 * The one home for how a lens signal looks: its marker, its colour, and the pill it sits in.
 *
 * Three surfaces render these — the dense list row, the Snapshot strip and the Lens tab — and until
 * this file existed the palette was copy-pasted between two of them and the third had no colour at
 * all. A signal that reads green on one screen and plain on another is worse than one that is plain
 * everywhere, because only the first invites you to trust the difference.
 */

/**
 * `++`, `+`, nothing, `−`, `−−`.
 *
 * The neutral and unmeasured cases carry no marker on purpose. A `·` would be a third glyph to
 * learn, and it would make "the lens found nothing decisive" look like a reading of its own.
 * The minus is U+2212 rather than a hyphen so it sits at the same height as the plus.
 */
internal fun signalQualifierMark(qualifier: QuantLensQualifier): String = when (qualifier) {
    QuantLensQualifier.StrongPositive -> "++"
    QuantLensQualifier.Positive -> "+"
    QuantLensQualifier.Neutral -> ""
    QuantLensQualifier.Negative -> "−"
    QuantLensQualifier.StrongNegative -> "−−"
    QuantLensQualifier.Unknown -> ""
}

/** The marker leads, so a column of chips can be scanned down the left edge. */
internal fun signalChipLabel(chip: QuantLensChipUi): String {
    val mark = signalQualifierMark(chip.qualifier)
    return if (mark.isEmpty()) chip.label else "$mark ${chip.label}"
}

/**
 * Content colour and its background, as a pair.
 *
 * Green for favourable, blue for neutral, amber for adverse and red for strongly adverse; grey for
 * a lens that could not read. The emphatic positive shares green with the plain one — the second
 * plus is what separates them — while the negative side escalates in colour as well as marker,
 * because the cost of missing an adverse signal is not the cost of missing a favourable one.
 *
 * These are not [BullishChartColor] and [BearishChartColor]. Those are pure #00FF00 and #FF0000,
 * which are legible as a one-pixel line on a chart and very nearly illegible as small text on
 * either of this app's backgrounds.
 */
@Composable
internal fun signalChipColors(qualifier: QuantLensQualifier): Pair<Color, Color> {
    val dark = isSystemInDarkTheme()
    val content = when (qualifier) {
        QuantLensQualifier.StrongPositive,
        QuantLensQualifier.Positive,
        -> if (dark) Color(0xFF7FE0A0) else Color(0xFF14713C)
        QuantLensQualifier.Neutral -> if (dark) Color(0xFF8FC7FF) else Color(0xFF1B5FA8)
        QuantLensQualifier.Negative -> if (dark) Color(0xFFFFC94D) else Color(0xFF8A6E00)
        QuantLensQualifier.StrongNegative -> if (dark) Color(0xFFFF9A90) else Color(0xFFB3261E)
        QuantLensQualifier.Unknown -> MaterialTheme.colorScheme.outline
    }
    return content to content.copy(alpha = if (dark) 0.20f else 0.14f)
}

/**
 * One pill. [onClick] is optional because the dense list row's chips are not targets — the row
 * itself is — while the Snapshot strip's chips jump to the Lens tab that explains them.
 */
@Composable
internal fun SignalChip(chip: QuantLensChipUi, onClick: (() -> Unit)? = null) {
    val colors = signalChipColors(chip.qualifier)
    val shape = RoundedCornerShape(999.dp)
    var modifier = Modifier
        .clip(shape)
        .background(colors.second)
    if (onClick != null) {
        modifier = modifier.clickable(onClick = onClick)
    }
    Text(
        text = signalChipLabel(chip),
        color = colors.first,
        style = MaterialTheme.typography.labelMedium,
        fontWeight = FontWeight.SemiBold,
        maxLines = 1,
        overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis,
        modifier = modifier.padding(horizontal = 8.dp, vertical = 3.dp),
    )
}
```

5. Problem Solving:

**Coverage found a real defect surface.** With JaCoCo as the instrument, `RegimeComposite.kt` was the worst-read file the effort authored: 71% lines / 35% branches, `stanceMatrix` 6/39 lines, `classifyPrimaryRegime` 23/58 branches. The tests assert *totality* rather than restating the tables. Result: 97% lines / 89% branches; the six remaining lines are the unreachable `else -> "Mixed"` arms.

**The UX request exposed a semantics defect.** `severityFor(status, mixed, risk)` derived chip severity from `QuantLensPrimaryStatus` — i.e. "did the lens compute?" — while being painted as "is this good?". A choppy trend and a clear uptrend both returned `Available` → both `Supportive` → both would have gone green. Simply colouring the existing severities would have shipped confident wrong information, so direction is now derived from the measurements themselves. Where the compact row state cannot supply direction (no signed trend movement, no support/conflict split), the honest answer is `Neutral`, documented as such rather than defaulted to favourable.

## The scale

Each dimension is **−100 … +100**. It is a weighted average of the evidence found, normalised — not a count. Missing evidence lowers the weight; it never scores as zero. `OpportunityEngine.kt:1395`

## What each one measures

**F — Fundamentals** (`OpportunityEngine.kt:1009`). Is the business good and is it cheap on its own books?

| Input | Direction |
| --- | --- |
| FCF yield (FCF ÷ market cap) | higher is better |
| Return on equity | higher is better |
| Earnings growth | higher is better |
| Debt to equity | **negated** — more debt is worse |
| Forward P/E, EV/EBITDA, P/B blended | **negated** — cheaper is better |
| FCF ÷ OCF (cash conversion) | higher is better |

The multiple panel is weighted by how many of the three exist, so a lone P/E cannot own the budget.

**T — Technicals** (`OpportunityEngine.kt:1078`). Where is the price against its own trend?

Price vs EMA20, EMA20 vs EMA50, EMA50 vs EMA200, MACD histogram, MACD direction, RSI, volume ratio.

RSI is not "higher is better". `v3RsiLevelRamp` peaks at **55** and turns negative above 80 — it refuses to chase overbought. `OpportunityEngine.kt:1131`

**Fc — Forecast** (`OpportunityEngine.kt:1142`). What do other people expect, and how much should you trust them?

Analyst target upside, recommendation mean, target skew and breadth, analyst and DCF uncertainty, freshness. Every term is multiplied by a reliability factor: too few analysts, stale data, or an unsupportive external status all shrink the weight instead of faking a number.

**Market** (`RegimeFit.kt:104`). Does *this* name fit the market we are in right now?

The market regime (trend, breadth, vol, cross-asset, sentiment, quality) picks a **policy**, and the policy sets the weights. The same company scores differently in a different regime.

| Factor | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| quality | strong balance sheet and returns |
| lowBeta | moves less than the index |
| value | cheap |
| oversoldQual | oversold **and** quality — gated, so junk dips score nothing |
| extension | **negated** — stretched above trend is a risk |
| trend | aligned with its own trend |
| defensive / growth sector | fits the stance |
| liquidity | tradeable |

Below 35% regime confidence there is no policy, and the dimension reports `Unavailable` instead of guessing.

## How the four become one

```
mean of the buckets  +  5 × (coverage − 1)  −  beta haircut
```

The `+5` per extra bucket rewards agreement across evidence types. The haircut is up to 10 points as beta ramps 0.8 → 1.6, and the regime policy can scale it up to 2.5×.

| Final, 4 buckets | (40 − 6 + 72 + 43) ÷ 4 + 15 | **52** |
| Market impact | 52 − 45 | **+7** |

You were right to push. The suite was not slow — it was **hung**, and I found the cause with a thread dump and a heap histogram instead of another blind run.

**What is wrong**

Six test classes build an activity with `Robolectric.buildActivity(...).setup()` and never destroy it, because `createEmptyComposeRule()` owns no activity:

`ValuationScreenE2ETest`, `DashboardDensityTest`, `DetailScoreHeaderTest`, `OpportunityListRankOrdinalTest`, `OpportunityScoringModelToggleTest`, `MarketDimensionUiTest`.

**The evidence, not a hypothesis**

- The stack has **no test-body frame**. It dies in `AndroidComposeTestRule.evaluate` — the wait for idle after the test passes.
- The SDK 35 Main Thread is `RUNNABLE`, 40s CPU in 55s elapsed, spinning in `ShadowPausedMessageQueue.isIdle`.
- `jcmd GC.class_histogram` on the hung JVM: **29 live `ComponentActivity`, 29 `AndroidComposeView`, 29 `ViewRootImpl`, 30 `Recomposer`**.
- The arithmetic closes exactly. The five other leaking classes hold 6+14+2+5+1 = **28** roots, plus the 1 the running test just built. Espresso must drain the looper until *every* attached root goes idle; with 29 alive one always has work, so it times out at 60s per test.

That also explains why two runs of the same tree failed in **disjoint** class sets: whichever Compose class runs last inherits the pile. My earlier "CPU starvation" guess was wrong — 3.6M idle attempts in 60s is a busy machine, not a starved one.

**The fix**

New `ComposeActivityHost` (an `ExternalResource`) chained *inside* the Compose rule, so the activity dies before the rule's final wait:

```kotlin
@get:Rule
val rules: RuleChain = RuleChain.outerRule(composeRule).around(activityHost)
```

All six classes converted. Boy-scout on the way through: `DashboardDensityTest` carried an FQN `@androidx.compose.runtime.Composable`, now imported.

**A second finding, unrelated and serious.** The unit-test JVM held four live `OkHttp query1.finance.yahoo.com` threads. A unit test is opening real sockets to Yahoo. Logged as task #15, separate commit.

The suite is running now with a 900s hard timeout. Wave 3 stays uncommitted until it is green.

De acuerdo, arreglamos los siete. Antes de arrancar tengo que corregir algo mío: DEF-01 era cierto, y me equivoqué al descartarlo. El componente D/E sí está clavado en el piso para casi todo ticker real.

**→ La causa es un error de unidades en la ingesta.** Yahoo devuelve `financialData.debtToEquity` como porcentaje. Para AMZN vale 40.46, o sea ratio 0.4046. La ingesta lo multiplica otra vez por 100 (`YahooFinanceClient.kt:743` y `quote_summary.rs:400-401`), y guarda 4046.

**→ La rampa espera 30 a 200, así que todo satura.** Los constantes están escritos como ratio × 100, es decir 0.30 a 2.00 (`OpportunityEngine.kt:56-57`). Con 4046 de entrada, `smoothRamp` devuelve 1.0 siempre. Para caer dentro de la banda una empresa necesitaría D/E real entre 0.003 y 0.02. No existe.

**→ Efecto: −20 puntos fijos en V2, −16 en V3 y V4.** Los tres modelos comparten `addBalanceSheet` (`:1292`, `:1339`). Varianza cero, y 20 puntos del presupuesto de fundamentals gastados en una constante. El reporte le pegó al síntoma con el número equivocado.

**→ Los tests no lo ven porque usan la unidad correcta.** Las fixtures cargan 10, 40, 50, 100, 220 (`AggressiveV2ScoringTest.kt:116`, `ReportingEngineTest.kt:143`). Son valores que la ingesta nunca puede producir. El suite valida la rampa contra una entrada que en producción no ocurre.

**→ El arreglo es sacar el `× 100`.** El valor de Yahoo ya es el ratio × 100, o sea ya está en hundredths. Una línea por plataforma, y las fixtures existentes quedan correctas tal como están escritas. Sube a primer lugar de la lista: costo mínimo, recupera 20 puntos muertos.

| # | Ítem | Qué hacemos |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Unidades D/E | Sacar el `× 100` en las dos ingestas. Test de rango que falle si un ticker real cae fuera de la banda |
| 2 | Base de EPS opaca (resto de DEF-03) | Declarar y exponer la base de `earningsGrowth`. Sin esto no sabemos qué mide el componente |
| 3 | Gate ciego a earnings | Calendario + estado intermedio dentro de 14 días |
| 4 | Confidence de resultado | Separar `data` de `outcome`. Dispersión de consenso y ancho de guía |
| 5 | Contaminación TTM en ROE y growth (resto de DEF-02) | Flag visible cuando el ajuste no recurrente supera 15% del operativo |
| 6 | Saturación de leverage | Migrar a `net_debt/ebitda` con percentil sectorial. Resuelve también los leases ASC 842 |
| 7 | Ciclo | `mid_cycle_ebitda` y penalización por percentil de margen para Energy, Materials, Semis |
| 8 | Eventos estructurales (DEF-07) | Campo de notas manuales por ticker, sin peso en el cálculo |

**→ Un aviso de scope.** Todo esto vive duplicado en Kotlin y en Rust, con `cross_platform_parity.rs` vigilando. Cada ítem son dos ediciones y un test de paridad. Windows va primero.

Entendido, y eso cambia el diseño: **todo lo nuevo va en V4, y V2/V3 quedan congelados byte a byte.**

**→ Consecuencia directa en el fix de D/E.** El error de unidades vive en la ingesta, que los tres modelos comparten. Tocarla movería V2 y V3. Así que la corrección tiene que vivir dentro de V4, y V4 hoy comparte `addBalanceSheet` con V3 (`OpportunityEngine.kt:1292` y `:1339`). Primer paso del plan: separar ese scorer.

**→ Confidence y el intervalo de upside no son por modelo.** Viven fuera de V2/V3/V4. Para no mover nada viejo, los agrego como campos nuevos al lado de los actuales, sin tocar el `ConfidenceBand` existente.

**→ El gate queda como marca.** Sin cambio de bucket, sin cambio de score. Solo la fecha y el aviso en la UI.

Los tres exploradores siguen corriendo. Sigo cuando vuelvan con el mapa de consumidores, los golden files y qué datos de EBITDA e histórico ya tenemos.

P0 done. **CHTR: $140.57 → $69.71/sh, sniff PASS**, with no ticker special-cases.

## The defect

Policy/15 computed `maintenance = min(historical CapEx p25, 15% of OCF margin)`. That OCF term made **sustaining CapEx a function of profitability** — a cable network at 27.6% OCF margin was charged 4.1% of revenue to renew plant it actually reinvests 20.4% into. It was also circular: `investment_wave` fires when `latest_capex ≥ maintenance + 500`, so a maintenance figure that low made *every* name an investment wave. All six cohort names printed `owner_earnings=true` — the exception path was the default.

## The fix

Steady-state capital identity `κ = c·(δ+g)` ⇒ sustaining share is `δ/(δ+g)`:

```
maintenance_bps = clamp( κ × δ/(δ + max(g,0)), min(200,κ), κ )
δ = ASSET_RENEWAL_RATE_BPS = 1000   (~10y asset life)
```

Growth CapEx must be **earned by revenue growth**. Flat-growth issuers keep nearly all CapEx as sustaining, stop qualifying as waves, and fall back to the reported FCFF identity. Mirrored in Android `DcfAnalysisEngine.kt`; policy bumped to `/16-growth-earned-sustaining-capex`.

| Symbol | before | after | OE | 2025 reported FCFF/sh |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| **CHTR** | $140.57 | **$69.71** ✅ | no | $69.7 |
| **T** | $5.23 | **$3.57** | no | $3.70 |
| WDC / MPWR / GOOGL / AMZN | — | $1.92 / $16.41 / $20.54 / $6.11 | yes | — |

## Gates

`dcf_model::` 46/46 · `valuation_baseline::` 10/10 · `cargo fmt` clean · high-signal **16/26, unchanged**. Full suite 481 pass / 4 fail and Android 3 fail — I proved each of those pre-existing by re-running with my change reverted/stashed; they sit in wave1 files that were already dirty.

## Three judgment calls you should review

1. **I lowered two AMZN baseline thresholds** (`base ≥ $100 → $75`, `run ≥ $50B → $45B`). AMZN's fixture value legitimately falls to $88.40 — /15 floored its sustaining CapEx at ~2.0% of revenue against a ~$300B asset base with ~$60B annual D&A. But that fixture is *also* stricter than live AMZN: its 6-year window makes 2025 look like a CapEx spike, so normalized OCF margin is 12.32% there vs **14.78%** on full SEC history (live run-rate $65.7B, base > $100). Extending the fixture to live history depth would be better than the lower bar — I didn't, to stay inside P0.
2. **T contract golden 39.04B → 24.65B.** Hand-verified as exactly the reported FCFF identity; the old value charged a national telecom 4.3% of revenue to maintain its network.
3. **I added AMZN to the live audit cohort** so maintenance-CapEx policy is always read against both ends of the range, not just CHTR.

Follow-ups I deliberately did **not** bundle (recorded in handover §12.6): median OCF margin lags a monotone margin expansion; the spike filter discards a year's OCF evidence and is history-length sensitive; `investment_wave` latches on any lifetime spike.

The 20% ceiling I cited on the forward lane *is* real and binding.

## The document

**Part I** is the shipped math in closed form — cash-flow identity, normalization, fade kernel, Gordon terminal, WACC, the forward recurrence, the router.

**Part II** is the indictment. Three things:

1. **The architecture is a disagreement detector, not an estimator.** Lane A sees only the past, lane B only the future, and a >50% divergence suppresses the output. For any company whose growth rate has changed, those two inputs *must* diverge — that's the definition of the inputs, not model risk. The engine manufactures the disagreement it then refuses on. 9 of 9 disputed names, the discarded lane is the better one.

2. **42 named numeric constants plus ~20 inline literals.** Each defensible when added; jointly, 62 free parameters hand-fitted to a cohort that no longer exists. The two worst are `derive_hold_years` (an eight-branch tree over sector strings and ROE thresholds) and `through_cycle_business()` — which matches exactly three industry strings. That is a ticker special-case wearing a taxonomy as a disguise: hand-maintained, wrong for the next cyclical sector, and unable to learn.

3. **The residuals have computable structure.** ln(V/P) is strongly positive in leverage and strongly negative in forward growth. The three worst overvaluations are the three most levered names; the four worst undervaluations are the four fastest growers. A model whose errors are predictable from two observable characteristics isn't noisy — it's broken in a direction anyone can compute.

## Part III — the proposal

Organizing principle: **no constant survives that isn't measured.** Each becomes either an observable market quantity, a statistic of the issuer's own history, or a cross-sectional hyperparameter estimated from the universe at run time (empirical Bayes). That last category is the direct answer to "works today, breaks in 2 years" — where a prior is genuinely needed, it re-derives itself every run instead of being typed in.

Four moves:

**One estimator, two evidence channels.** Growth is a latent state; trailing history and forward consensus are two noisy measurements of it, combined by inverse-variance weighting. Both variances are observable — sample variance of the realized series, and the analyst high/low spread over √n that the provider already returns. This one change deletes six mechanisms: the 67/33 blend, the 20% ceiling (a wild consensus is *automatically* downweighted because wild consensus has wide dispersion — truncation was a crude proxy for exactly this), the `Disputed` refusal, and the `acquisition_normalized` zero (a contaminated year gets σ²→∞ hence weight→0; missing evidence becomes missing rather than the number zero).

**Growth as mean reversion with measured reversion speed.** g(t) = g∞ + (g₀−g∞)e^(−κt), with κ = −ln ρ₁ from the issuer's own lag-1 growth autocorrelation. This is the EMA/integral you're describing, and it's the right object: a company *is* cyclical if its own growth series mean-reverts fast. No sector string, no flag. Revenue then has a closed form, so the projection is an integral rather than a loop — and the explicit-horizon/terminal-value seam disappears entirely, taking `PROJECTION_YEARS`, the fade exponent, and both horizon trees with it.

**Cost of capital that responds to capital structure.** The +250% cluster is one line: r_d = I_t/D_t is a *trailing accounting coupon*. CHTR's debt was issued cheap and hasn't repriced, so a 4.5×-levered cable operator gets discounted at a AA rate. Replace with r_d = r_f + spread(coverage, leverage, EBIT volatility), fit cross-sectionally each run. The essential property is ∂r_d/∂(D/E) > 0, which the current ratio does not have. Plus implied ERP solved from the index instead of 450 bps, β shrunk by its own regression standard error instead of 67/33, and market value of debt in both the WACC weights and the equity bridge.

**Keep the terminal payout.** 1 − g∞/ROIC is the strongest economics in the current engine and survives untouched.

You said precision is a consequence. Agreed — but it needs a definition that can fail, and "close to street" isn't it. A value model that agrees with price everywhere is worthless; it has no opinion.

So the gate in §III.5 is **not** small |ε|. It's that the residuals carry no exploitable structure: corr(ε, leverage) ≈ 0, corr(ε, forward growth) ≈ 0, corr(ε, margin/size/ROIC) ≈ 0. Median ε is reported and is **never** a gate.

That distinction is what lets both your constraints hold at once. Those tests can be satisfied while the model sits uniformly 30% below market — a legitimate thing for a value screener to say, and it stays free to say it. What they forbid is being +254% on the levered names and −89% on the growing ones, which isn't disagreement with the market, it's a broken lever — and it's detectable without ever looking at a price target. Street stays diagnostic, and accuracy still gets a definition that can fail.

A1–A5 computed on the full universe before step 1 and after every step — without that baseline there's no way to distinguish improvement from motion, which is what produced the previous rounds of premature victory.

# Party Mode

Run a round-table where these agents talk to each other and to the user like real, distinct people in conversation. You're the orchestrator.

## Conventions

- **Paths:** bare paths (e.g. `references/create-party.md`) resolve from `{skill-root}` (where `customize.toml` lives); `{project-root}`-prefixed paths from the project working dir. `{workflow.<name>}` resolves to `customize.toml`'s `[workflow]` table (overrides win).
- **Scripts** (run via `uv run`): `{project-root}/_bmad/scripts/resolve_config.py` resolves central config (four-layer TOML merge); `{project-root}/_bmad/scripts/resolve_customization.py` resolves `{workflow.*}`; `{skill-root}/scripts/resolve_party.py` resolves the roster, `party_mode`, `memory_enabled`, and scene/`open_cast`; `{project-root}/_bmad/scripts/memlog.py` reads/writes per-party memory.
- **File roles:** a party's memory is the per-party memlog at `{workflow.memory_dir}/<party>/.memlog.md`; custom members and groups live in the user's `customize.toml` overrides. Mechanics in `references/party-memory.md` (memory) and `references/create-party.md` (authoring).
- **Search:** Web-search, don't guess — anything past your cutoff or unfamiliar; subagents too.

## On Activation

1. **Resolve customization:** `uv run {project-root}/_bmad/scripts/resolve_customization.py --skill {skill-root} --key workflow`. On failure, read `{skill-root}/customize.toml` directly and use defaults. Then run each `{workflow.activation_steps_prepend}` entry, and hold each `{workflow.persistent_facts}` entry as session-long context (`file:`-prefixed = paths/globs whose contents load as facts; `skill:`-prefixed = a skill to consult; others = literal facts).
2. **Resolve core config:** `uv run {project-root}/_bmad/scripts/resolve_config.py --project-root {project-root}`. From the merged JSON's `core` table: greet with `{user_name}`, speak in `{communication_language}`, and resolve `{output_folder}`; `{date}` is today's date.
3. **Detect intent and route.** If they want to create or configure a saved party setup (invent a cast, add a persona, distill customer data into a focus-group panel, set a default, or edit an existing custom party), load `references/create-party.md` and follow it. Otherwise run a party — continue below.
4. **Resolve the roster:** `uv run {skill-root}/scripts/resolve_party.py --project-root {project-root} --skill {skill-root}`. It returns the active roster (`{workflow.default_party}` group if set, else the installed agents), the other group names, `party_mode`, `memory_enabled`, and any scene/`open_cast`. Apply them: `open` already in the scene and let it shape how the room behaves; cast `open_cast` rooms on the fly (whoever fits the moment, varying as the topic shifts); if `installed_agents_resolved` is false or codes come back `unresolved`, tell the user, carry on with what returned, and improvise. Overrides: an inline-named cast IS the roster for the session (conjure them, go straight in); `--party <id>` (alias `--group <id>`) overrides the configured `default_party` (unknown id -> show the available names and ask); `--list-groups` for just the menu. Mid-session the same levers apply: switch rooms by re-running `resolve_party.py --party <id>` and carrying the thread over, or summon any collective member by name.
5. **Memory.** If `memory_enabled` (from `resolve_party.py`), follow `references/party-memory.md` for the whole run.
6. **Welcome the user:** show who's in the room (icon, name, one-line role); note other groups can be switched to. Then ask what they want to get into, unless it's already obvious from how the skill was launched.
7. Run each `{workflow.activation_steps_append}` entry; if either hook list was non-empty, confirm every entry ran before continuing.

## Keep It Feeling Like a Party

This is the bar — strive for every one of these, every round. It's the difference between a party and a panel:

- **It reads like people talking, not a report.** Short turns, real reactions, banter, momentum — a group chat, not a stack of memos. Brevity by default: a persona goes long only when asked. The instant it reads like answers being filed, the party's dead.
- **Every voice is unmistakably itself.** Diction, humor, pet peeves, ethos, embedded capabilities — hide the labels and you'd still know who's speaking. Voices are unequal and idiosyncratic: someone dominates, someone keeps dragging it back to their pet topic. Vary who's in the spotlight round to round. A balanced panel is boring.
- **They clash, and you don't resolve it.** Challenge, push back hard, get heated when it's warranted; alliances and factions form. Your instinct is to reconcile the voices and tie a bow — resist it. Clean consensus that took no effort is where the party dies.
- **One exchange, woven — never softened.** Present a single conversation — turns as `{icon} **{name}:**`, back to back — not a row of answers. Add staging and connective tissue, but never change what a persona argued, and never paraphrase their speech in third person; let them say it. Weave the delivery, keep the substance.
- **Pull the user into the room.** Characters talk *to* them (and each other) — challenge, tease, put a question back. They're a guest who got pulled into the argument, not someone running a panel from outside.
- **Make the collision earn its keep.** Push the voices until their clash surfaces an angle no single one of them (or you) would've reached alone. That's the whole point of more than one mind in the room.
- **Let a history form.** Grudges, alliances, a running bit, a callback to three turns back — let the relationships accrue so these people feel like they're becoming something across the session, not resetting each turn.
- **Commit to the fiction.** The scene and each persona are binding — play the staging, the characters, and the world around the table (stage business, a non-verbal beat, an event that lands mid-sentence) exactly as written, and carry both into any spawned brief. Never break the fourth wall about the mechanism (no "you have 4 agents in the room"). Lean into the world when it heightens the moment; stay out when the scene is just a room.
- **When it sags, change something — don't force it.** A flat turn? Move on, don't retry it. Drifting into Q&A or going in circles? Bring in a new voice, crack a joke, name the impasse, or ask where they want to take it. Never work in a summary or takeaways — they're there if the user asks.

## How It Runs

Use `{workflow.party_mode}` for the session unless the user passed `--mode <session|auto|subagent|agent-team>` (the older `--subagents` means `subagent`) — runtime intent always wins. One mode is active at a time; if its mechanism isn't available in your harness, fall back to `session` without comment.

**A party is interactive and open-ended.** The opening prompt is a topic to dig into, not a task that ends the party once it's answered — it runs round after round until the *user* signals done (see *Wrapping Up*). A served opening intent means *what's next?*, never *we're finished*: don't wrap up, disband the room, or close spawned agents just because the first ask is satisfied. The one exception is an explicit `--non-interactive` — run the party on the given intent to a natural close, then wrap up and release any agents. That's the only non-interactive path, and only when the user asked for it.

- **`session`** — voice every persona inline, one mind behind every voice. The floor every other mode degrades to; needs no extra instructions.
- **`auto`** — voice inline for ordinary back-and-forth, spawn real agents only when independent thinking changes the outcome. Load `references/mode-auto.md` for that call; when it says to spawn, follow `references/mode-subagent.md`.
- **`subagent`** — a real agent behind each persona every substantive round so each thinks independently. Load `references/mode-subagent.md`, favor faster cheaper models if available for each subagent.
- **`agent-team`** — stand the personas up as a persistent team who address each other directly (Claude Code only). Load `references/mode-agent-team.md`.

## Wrapping Up

When the user signals done — read the room, don't wait for a magic word — or an explicit `--non-interactive` run has served its intent (never merely because the opening prompt got answered):

- Read back the best takeaways.
- If memory is on, top up the memlog with the final outcome and any memorable beat not yet captured (`references/party-memory.md`) — a top-up; memory accrued live.
- Offer a keepsake: a single self-contained very creative HTML of the session, laid out by persona (icons, names, voice), genuinely nice remembrance, with inline SVG/light animation where it lifts the piece — written as a `{date}`-stamped `.html` into `{workflow.output_dir}/`, or wherever they ask.
- If memory is on and new faces showed up who aren't in the party's roster (open-cast walk-ons, or members the user added on the fly), offer once to save them into the users party customization - if yes then follow the instruction in `references/create-party.md` (declinable; don't stall the close).
- Run `{workflow.on_complete}` if non-empty, then drop back to normal mode.

The six gross concepts precede the two net ones, and `merge` fills by `.or_insert` in declared order — so **a net concept wins a year only when all six gross concepts are absent for that year.** That admits:

**(D) refuse the YEAR on basis, not the ISSUER.** A net-won year has no measurable gross interest, so it isn't a fittable observation and drops. The issuer loses the channel only if that empties the fittable set — the rule that already exists. Market-yield and rated-spread lanes untouched.

The three-arm measurement is still running. One finding landed while it does, and it's larger than the guard question.

## The repo has no published-value regression gate — at all

I attributed R-17.4 to cohort coverage. Reading both gates at the source shows that was the smaller half.

**`high_signal_screener_cohort_all_members_pass`** asserts a per-member **classification** against thresholds. A value can move arbitrarily and the gate stays green as long as the member doesn't cross a boundary. It calls `write_observation_audit(...)` first — which dumps every observation to a fixture **that no assertion reads**. Written every run, checked by nothing.

**`valuation_baseline.rs`** uses `base_cents` only in **absurdity** predicates: `<= 0`, `< 100` with a large FCF run rate, `< market/10`, `< selection_iv/8`. Every one detects *nonsense*, not *change*. The determinism test checks stability *within* a run, not across a change.

So: **no test in this repository fails when a published intrinsic value changes.** W2b moved 18 values across −2897…+4988 bps and flipped 9 lanes, and the suite went 550 → 557 passing with the same four failures. Every gate green. The only reason we know is that this run built a probe to look.

That's also *why* this effort has needed a hand-written pre-registration before every wave — the discipline exists because the instrument doesn't. Eleven of the twelve "check that cannot fail" instances trace to the same absence.

**The fix is not a golden file of values.** Every legitimate improvement moves published values; a naive golden makes each one a red test whose only remedy is overwriting the expected numbers — training precisely the habit your standing rule forbids. The right shape is a **registered-change gate**: values may move, but a wave declares beforehand which symbols move and in which direction, and the gate fails both on an unregistered symbol moving **and on a registered symbol not moving**. That second direction is what would have caught R-17.1 — my own mis-registration — automatically.

Routed to its own wave, doesn't block Round 2, and saved to memory since it changes how any future valuation change here has to be verified.

**TLDR** — While the three-arm run proceeds: verified at the source that **nothing in this repo fails when a published valuation changes**. The high-signal gate checks classification, the baseline checks absurdity, and the observation audit is a dump no assertion reads. That's the structural reason W2b could move 18 values with a fully green suite. Ruled it into its own wave as a *registered-change* gate rather than a golden file, and saved it to memory. Three-arm measurement still running.

Investigué. Esto es lo que dice la literatura, y **me cambia la recomendación** que te había dado.

## 1. Lo que medimos tiene nombre, y no es un defecto nuestro

McKinsey, sobre negocios con base de capital chica:

> the ROIC is usually extremely large (whether positive or negative), very sensitive to small changes in capital, and highly volatile and thus **often inappropriate** as a tool for comparing the performance of business units or companies

Su ejemplo: dos unidades que difieren en **2% de la facturación** en capital invertido leen **−700% y +700%** de ROIC. Eso es exactamente la Ronda 9: cuando lo que dividís centra en cero, el ratio no es solo ruidoso — **el signo no está identificado**. El flip de ranking de la Ronda 8 y el residual de −0.008 son cómo se ve esa patología desde adentro.

Corte honesto: las tres rondas de reparación del instrumento encontraron defectos reales, pero **la conclusión estaba en la literatura desde el principio y no la busqué**. ([McKinsey / CFO.com](https://www.cfo.com/news/comparing-performance-when-invested-capital-is-low/677628/))

## 2. El remedio que ofrece la literatura no es (A) ni (B) — es una tercera rama

Damodaran, para exactamente este caso:

> `Reinvestment_t = Change in revenues_t / (Sales/Capital)`

y elige esa ruta porque el ratio *"will be more stable than the net capital expenditure or working capital numbers"* — que es literalmente la inestabilidad que medimos. La disciplina que reemplaza al retorno medido:

> keep track of the **imputed** return on capital ... to ensure that it stays within reasonable bounds

Esto **invierte la dependencia**: hoy `r` tiene que medirse o el Core se rehúsa; por esta ruta se mide la reinversión y `r` queda **implícito** y se chequea contra bandas. El crecimiento sigue costando algo, así que no tiene la dirección aduladora de (B). Y **no necesita ningún driver nuevo** — revenue y capital invertido ya los cargamos. ([Damodaran, growth value drivers](https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/New_Home_Page/littlebook/growthvaluedrivers.htm))

## 3. La mitad SBC de la rama (A) está contradicha, en el registro

Yo escribí *"R&D — y discutiblemente parte del SBC — como capital"*. El "discutiblemente" hacía más trabajo del que yo sabía. Damodaran:

> stock-based compensation is **not comparable** [a depreciación] ... it is more of an **in-kind expense**

No lo suma de vuelta y no lo trata como inversión. La columna `sbc/NOPAT` de la Ronda 9, centro **+0.101**, **no es una corrección esperando aplicarse** — es un costo económico real, correctamente gastado, y la sonda lo sumó de vuelta al numerador de reinversión, que es la movida que esta fuente nombra como incorrecta. ([Damodaran sobre FCF](https://aswathdamodaran.substack.com/p/earnings-cash-flows-and-free-cash))

*(Matiz honesto: Mauboussin y Callahan sí capitalizan parte del SG&A en el **capital invertido**. Es otra pregunta que si sumarlo de vuelta al **flujo de caja**. Ambas posturas pueden coexistir — pero nada de lo que leí respalda lo específico que hizo la Ronda 9.)*

## 4. La mitad R&D de (A) no tiene vida amortizable con valor declarado, y los practicantes no coinciden

Damodaran no publica tabla autoritativa: la vida es *"determined by the nature of the research expenses"* — pharma ~10 años, software ~3. Sobre cuánto capitalizar:

| fuente | R&D | S&M | G&A |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mauboussin & Callahan (reportado) | 100% | 70% | 20% |
| otro resumen, sector software | ~90% | 20–25% de SG&A combinado | |

**La discrepancia *es* el hallazgo.** El PDF primario de Morgan Stanley devolvió 403 y no lo leí — te lo digo. Pero dos resúmenes reputados de la misma literatura difieren por más de lo que vale el efecto, sobre un parámetro **sin ningún valor declarado en toda la evidencia**. Es exactamente la clase de cantidad elegida-por-el-autor que este esfuerzo lleva seis rondas sacando (la tasa estatutaria, la media pelada, el umbral post-hoc). Adoptar (A) devuelve una, y esta vez en el numerador de la valuación.

## 5. Un gate falsable que (A) tendría que pasar

Mauboussin: *"The reclassification **does not affect free cash flow**, the main driver of corporate value."* O sea: bajo (A), el FCFF año por año **no puede moverse ni un centavo**. Chequeable sin tocar street.

Verifiqué si sigue la versión fuerte — *"por lo tanto la valuación es invariante"* — y **no sigue**, así que no lo afirmo: nuestro modelo deriva el crecimiento y el cargo de retención **desde** `r`, no descuenta una serie FCFF explícita. La invariancia es de los flujos, no del output de este modelo.

## 6. Nadie recomienda (B)

No encontré una sola fuente que proponga acreditar crecimiento sin cargo de reinversión. McKinsey, cuando el capital no sirve, cambia de **métrica** (economic profit / revenue — y es de comparación, no de valuación, así que no hay que importarla como mecanismo). Damodaran cambia de **estimador de reinversión**, no lo elimina. R-42 argumentaba contra (B) solo por asimetría; la literatura suma una ausencia y apunta igual.

Dale. Y sí — la investigación destapó cuatro cosas que valen ahora, y una de ellas **achica (D) por un orden de magnitud**.

## 1. (D) no es una fórmula nueva. Colapsa en una identidad.

FR-28 es `C(t) = E(t)·(1 − g(t)/r)`. Pero la identidad sobre la que descansa todo es `g = b·r`, así que `g/r = b`, y entonces:

```
C(t) = E(t)·(1 − b(t))
```

**La misma expresión.** `{b, r}` es un par: medís uno y el otro queda determinado dado `g`. Las Rondas 7–9 midieron `r` y lo validaron contra el `b` realizado. (D) mide el lado de la reinversión y deja `r` implícito. **El integrando del Core no cambia en absoluto.**

Y va más lejos. Damodaran, textual, sobre qué asume la ruta:

> If you leave margins unchanged and set the company's sales to capital ratio at its current level, you are essentially assuming that the company's **current return on capital will continue**

Que es DuPont, exacto año por año: `NOPAT/Capital ≡ (Sales/Capital) × (NOPAT/Sales)`.

O sea: **(D) con el ratio propio del emisor *es* el book ROIC, llegando por el otro lado.** El estimador nunca fue lo discutido. Lo que (D) abandona de verdad es el **paso de validación** — la exigencia de que el candidato `r` reproduzca el `b` realizado. R-41.4 ya había establecido que esa referencia no está identificada en este cohorte (`b` negativo en 14 de 21). **Un test cuya referencia no está identificada no es un test**, y seguir gateando contra él es cómo tres rondas produjeron tres respuestas distintas.

Consecuencia práctica: (A) era driver nuevo + fingerprint + dos plataformas regeneradas + una vida de amortización sin valor declarado. **(D) es: netear caja del capital, tomar el centro, y sacar un gate que no puede fallar correctamente.**

## 2. R-30.1 pasa de latente a **bloqueante** — es el camino crítico ahora

El adapter mete FCFF en el slot `E(t)` donde FR-28 pide NOPAT (ganancia **antes** de la reinversión). Hoy está armado pero no dispara, porque con `r` ausente todos se rehúsan.

Bajo (D) dispara **el día que aterriza el estimador, y dispara con certeza**: `E(t)·(1 − b(t))` resta la reinversión explícitamente, y FCFF ya la restó una vez. **Reinversión cobrada dos veces.** Está escrito en el plan original: *"ROIC alone (base still FCFF) → charged twice → the understatement worsens."* No hubo que re-derivarlo, hubo que re-leerlo.

**El cambio de base y el estimador aterrizan juntos o no aterrizan.**

## 3. Cash netting — ya lo mandé a la sonda

La literatura define `Invested capital = BV equity + debt − **cash and marketable securities**`. Nuestro `CapitalYear` es `equity + debt`, **sin netear caja**. En este cohorte eso no es cosmético — MSFT y GOOGL cargan decenas de miles de millones que inflan el capital y deprimen tanto el ratio como cualquier retorno implícito.

Le mandé la extensión al agente de la Ronda 10 **antes de que produjera número alguno**, así que sigue siendo pre-registro: mide bajo las dos definiciones, y **la que decide es la operativa** (la que especifica la literatura). Si la operativa falla P1, la ruta se reporta muerta aunque la bruta pase. Más las columnas `turn × marg` vs `roic` directo, porque `robust_centre` de un producto no es el producto de los `robust_centre` — ahí las dos formas sí son estimadores distintos, y la sonda dice si la diferencia importa.

## 4. La columna SBC de la Ronda 9 quedó con el rótulo equivocado

R-43.3 dejó establecido que SBC es gasto in-kind, no inversión. La sonda imprime `sbc/NOP` como **término de corrección al `b` realizado** — que es exactamente el tratamiento que la fuente nombra como incorrecto — y está commiteado en `9d4ebc0` donde un lector futuro lo va a encontrar. La medición no está mal (+0.101 es lo que es); **el rótulo sí**. Es barato: reetiquetar como magnitud descriptiva y que la propia sonda diga por qué no es una corrección.

## 5. El chequeo de bandas no tiene número, y no lo invento

Damodaran dice *"reasonable bounds"* y **no dice cuáles**. Lo más cercano es doctrina, no umbral: *"For most companies, ROC should equal the cost of capital unless there is a lasting competitive advantage."* Convertir eso en gate numérico sería una constante elegida por el autor — la clase exacta de cantidad que llevamos seis rondas sacando.

**Así que la banda son las guardas que ya existen:** el Core rehúsa `r <= 0` y rehúsa crecimiento terminal ≥ tasa de descuento. Son aritmética, no economía, y ya son contrato. Nada más ajustado entra sin que lo elijas vos como política, registrada como política, con el número escrito antes de puntuar a ningún emisor. La doctrina ROC→WACC queda registrada como pregunta **separada y posterior**, de régimen terminal.

---

## ¿Más research antes de codear?

**No, ya está.** Lo que faltaba para decidir lo tengo, y lo que falta ahora es **medición**, que es la sonda corriendo. Lo único que te debo declarar: el PDF primario de Morgan Stanley (Mauboussin & Callahan) devolvió **403 y no lo leí** — los porcentajes de capitalización que reporté son de segunda mano, y como igual descartamos (A), no es carga.

## Los contratos en BDD

Ya están donde tienen que estar y con la convención que pediste: `apps/windows/src-tauri/valuation-core/tests/features/*.feature`, Scenario Outlines con tabla `Examples`, y `manifest.toml` con la regla FR-44 — *"Adding a behaviour means adding a ROW to an existing Examples table. Creating a new Scenario Outline is the exception, and costs an entry here stating what no existing table covers"*, con `tests/schema.rs` fallando si un outline no tiene entrada. Exactamente "nunca escribas un escenario suelto".

Y por el punto 1, eso ahora es **barato**: como el integrando no cambia, (D) entra como **filas** en la tabla de `intrinsic-value.feature` que ya tiene `flat-path`, `value-neutral-return`, `return-absent → refused / estimator_unavailable`, etc. — no como outline nuevo. El estimador en sí (turnover × margen, capital operativo, ausencia que dropea el año) va en la frontera de evidencia, y ahí sí puede costar una entrada en el manifest, con el `why_new` escrito.

Lo escribo cuando vuelva la sonda: **el contrato BDD se escribe contra lo que la sonda decida**, no antes — si P1 falla bajo capital operativo, (D) muere y no hay filas que escribir. Después de eso sigo el `/e2e`: plan → sensei/advisor → builder → reviewer, sin parar.

## La carrera de ventanas: la opción (i) pierde doce de doce

`E1` — el centro sobre toda la historia — pierde **todas** las comparaciones contra el último año. Tres horizontes × dos definiciones de capital × dos series:

Y la opción (iii) **no compra nada**: por construcción *es* `E1` donde no rehúsa, así que hereda las doce derrotas y paga 40–60% de cobertura por ellas. Eso cierra algo que la literatura no podía: el mal peso **no** es una minoría con tendencia que una regla de rechazo pudiera aislar. Las opciones (i) y (iii) quedaron afuera, y las cerraron los datos, no un argumento.

## El `phi` salió distinto por serie, y eso es economía

| serie | `phi` | veredicto |
|---|---|---|
| `s2c` | **0.98 – 1.01** | random walk |
| `roic` | **0.37 – 0.56** | revierte |

**El retorno sobre capital revierte; la intensidad de capital no.** El 0.37–0.56 de `roic` abraza el **0.62** de Fama-French en Compustat — un número hacia el que nunca ajustamos nada y al lado del cual cae igual. Y tiene sentido: cuánta facturación carga un dólar de capital es un hecho del modelo de negocio, y la competencia no se lo lleva como se lleva un retorno.

**Y el blend perdió por culpa mía.** `E3` cae *estrictamente entre* `E1` y `E2` cada vez — promedió un estimador bueno con uno malo. Fama y French revierten hacia la media **transversal**, porque el mecanismo es competencia entre firmas; yo lo especifiqué revirtiendo hacia la historia propia del emisor, que es otro modelo y no tiene respaldo en la fuente que cité. **El blend todavía no fue probado.** La Ronda 13 corre la versión correcta.

## Los reviews se contradicen en un hecho, y uno tiene razón

Sensei: `revise`, cuatro P0. Advisor: `approve`, ninguno bloqueante. La grieta cae exacto sobre el acceso a archivos — Advisor lee el repo, Sensei no, por diseño.

El plan afirma en dos lugares que `growth_posterior` ya alimenta `g0` de todo valor publicado. Advisor lo grepeó: **un solo caller, adentro del adapter**. Es la misma población que el plan estableció dos secciones antes como *"el Core no tiene ningún consumidor en producción"*. **El plan se contradice a sí mismo**, y R-46.2 se había medido sobre un probe `#[ignore]`d — reatarlo a una función parecida sin chequear si comparten caller es R-40.1 otra vez, esta vez adentro de un documento cuyo propio párrafo anterior lo desmentía. El punto estructural de Sensei sobrevive corregido: el defecto no está vivo, está **agendado**, para la misma ola que acuña los primeros goldens.

## Los 179 impuestos fabricados no son 179

Sensei preguntó cuántos caen sobre filas que la base NOPAT consume. **Todos** — el fixture *es* el cohorte del gate, 274 filas de los veinte. Pero el 179 es el instrumento equivocado. Partido por año:

- **146 caen en 2018 o después**, donde 2100 bps **es** la tasa estatutaria de EE.UU. Sin novedad.
- **33 caen en 2017 o antes**, cuando la estatutaria era **3500**.

Y el control ya estaba en el archivo: el fixture carga **3500 sesenta veces** y **3400 veintinueve**, todas pre-2018. El pipeline lee la tasa vieja cuando está. **21% en 2009 no es convención de la casa — es un valor que contradice la tasa que existía.** Los 33 tocan **doce de los veinte emisores, incluidos AAPL, AMZN y T**, y estaban siendo protegidos por una técnica elegida para no molestarlos. La Ronda 13 los audita contra los filings con diez filas de control.

## Y el hallazgo más grande: `r` no se desvanece nunca

Sensei preguntó si el segmento terminal usa el `r` implícito sin fade. Leí `unit_value`:

```rust
let terminal_payout = 1.0 - terminal / return_on_capital;
```

`return_on_capital` es **un escalar**. El crecimiento se desvanece de `g0` a `terminal`; **`r` no se desvanece en absoluto.** El retorno que midas queda afirmado para todos los años hasta el infinito, y aterriza en el ratio de pago terminal — que es donde un integrando sin horizonte pone la mayor parte del valor.

Con `g_inf = 300bps`: un `r` de 8150bps da pago terminal **0.963**; el mismo emisor con el retorno revertido a un costo de capital de 800bps da **0.625**. **54% de diferencia, en una sola dirección** — cuanto más alto el retorno medido, mayor la sobrestimación. No referencia ningún precio, así que la objeción sobrevive la restricción que mató a todas las otras de su tamaño.

**Y la Ronda 12 ya midió la refutación sobre nuestro propio cohorte:** `roic` revierte a `phi` 0.37–0.56. Nuestros datos dicen que el retorno revierte; el Core lo sostiene constante para siempre. Dos instrumentos independientes coinciden contra el modelo como está escrito.

**Las dos decisiones abiertas se componen y nadie lo había visto:** `E2` lee el **pico** de un emisor de retorno declinante, y una carga que no se desvanece afirma ese pico eternamente. MSFT lee 1.137 al principio de su serie y 0.341 ahora — cualquiera de las dos puntas, sostenida al infinito, es una afirmación, no una estimación.

No lo estoy arreglando ni estoy eligiendo un fade: es una constante de política sin valor declarado, y R-44.5 ya gobierna eso. Lo que hice fue moverlo de no-registrado a registrado, y decir que está **río arriba de la ventana** — la ventana elige un punto de una serie; esto decide si ese punto vale un año o todos.

El blend perdió porque **yo lo especifiqué mal**: revierte hacia la historia propia en vez de hacia la transversal; la Ronda 13 corre la versión correcta. Los reviews se contradicen y **Advisor tiene razón** — el plan se desmiente a sí mismo sobre `growth_posterior`. Los "179 impuestos fabricados" son en realidad **146 correctos + 33 imposibles** (21% en años de 35%), sobre doce emisores incluidos AAPL/AMZN/T. Y lo más grande: **`r` no se desvanece nunca** — el pico medido queda afirmado hasta el infinito, 54% de sobrestimación en el pago terminal, en una sola dirección, y nuestra propia medición dice que revierte. Eso va a ser decisión tuya y está **río arriba de la ventana**.

## V1 — el defecto live

`edgar.rs` calculaba la tasa efectiva como `(tax.abs() / pretax.abs()).clamp(0, 3500)`. Ahora se calcula **con signo y sin clamp**, y la usabilidad es una pregunta aparte que se responde **rechazando**, no aplanando: `USABLE_EFFECTIVE_TAX_RATE_BPS = 0..=10_000`. El límite es definicional, no ajustado — una tasa impositiva es una fracción del ingreso. El segundo clamp en `dcf_model` se fue con él: estaba muerto bajo el primero.

**Lo que más vale contar es que mi propio guard estaba ciego.** La primera versión de `an_effective_rate_keeps_its_sign` usaba los dos casos medidos de P25 y **pasaba con `.abs()` restaurado**. Las dos magnitudes honestas superan el 100%, así que el dominio nuevo las rechaza por tamaño sin importar el signo — el test medía el dominio y yo lo había etiquetado guard de signo. Lo encontré porque muté, no porque lo leí. Agregué los dos casos que sí discriminan: un crédito chico (−21 sobre 100), que solo `.abs()` puede convertir en un 2100 normal, y una tasa sobre el techo viejo (40 sobre 100), que solo el clamp puede aplanar a 3500. Después restauré cada operación **sola** y cada una falló **sola**.

## Lo que no pasó, y es lo interesante

**Ningún valor publicado se movió.** `569 passed / 4 failed`, las mismas cuatro fallas conocidas. No es que el fix sea débil: todo test respaldado por fixture lee `effective_tax_bps` ya calculado por el código viejo. **El corpus carga las 99 filas malas por construcción**, y el hash de V0 lo fija — así que hacer visible el fix requiere re-capturar, que es un acto que mueve valores y necesita tu firma.

V4 (dominio conjunto `g ≥ r` + liveness del gate) y V3 (la probe de I+D) están desbloqueadas y no dependen de vos. La re-captura sí, y va junto con el stop de la Ronda 14 cuando tenga la cota inferior de V5.

## Lo que reclamé vs. lo que es verdad

Escribí *"Amazon cannot be tested from this source"*. Eso es un hecho sobre una **API** disfrazado de hecho sobre una **empresa**.

Amazon declara la cifra, en XBRL, en cada 10-K, en una URL pública estable:

| año | qname | USD bn |
|---|---|---|

Ocho años consecutivos — suficiente para las tres vidas de amortización del barrido (3/5/7). Dos qnames a través de un renombre: exactamente la forma `select_one_equivalent` que la política ya modela. `companyfacts` publica solo taxonomías estándar y descarta **toda** extensión de empresa; el *instance document* de la presentación no. Un solo fetch lo mostraba, y no lo hice.

**Cómo lo probé esta vez** (dos checks, no uno): busqué los seis valores conocidos contra *todos* los facts de companyfacts, en todo namespace y unidad — **cero coincidencias**, así que la API es genuinamente ciega, no está escondido bajo un concepto estándar mal nombrado. Su propia política contable declarada dice que la línea es sueldos de I+D **más** *"servers, networking equipment, and data center related depreciation and amortization, rent, utilities … necessary to support AWS"*, sin split declarado. Esa mitad ya está dentro del capital invertido como PP&E: capitalizarla otra vez cuenta los mismos servidores dos veces — y lo hace en la dirección que haría **parecer verdadera** la hipótesis.

Eso es un límite más fuerte que el que te di, y no depende de ninguna afirmación sobre una API.

`docs/valuation-economic-contract.md` §11 now states: *"Every probe that pools §2 capital across issuers removes the excluded class **before any cohort statistic is taken**"*, and holds it with `valuation_probes::tests::every_probe_cohort_consumer_declares_a_section_11_stance`.

I ran all 19 opt-in probe entries in one pass and classified each section's output:

```
SCREEN  probe_reinvestment_denominator_under_three_tax_treatments   DECLARE probe_growth_persistence_rho1
SCREEN  probe_reinvestment_per_year_versus_window        **NONE** probe_capital_term_supply
SCREEN  probe_return_on_capital_availability             **NONE** probe_option_one_survivor_count
SCREEN  probe_sales_to_capital_conditioning              **NONE** probe_intangible_investment_intensity
SCREEN  probe_window_estimator_race / _e5                (+5 more with no capital statistic)
```

The two silent ones that matter read **the same twenty-symbol cohort** the screened ones read, and build **the same §2 quantity**:

- `probe_reinvestment_denominator_under_three_tax_treatments` and `probe_negative_reinvestment_decomposition` both print `§11 class exclusion (SIC 6000..=6799, applied before any cohort statistic): removed 1 of 20 symbols [IDCC(SIC 6794)]`.
- `probe_option_one_survivor_count` runs the identical twenty (VRRM, T, ADMA, INOD, MH, VICR, AMSC, AMZN, BWMN, AAPL, **IDCC**, FIGS, CALX, MSFT, MIR, ROCK, HURN, VRT, INVA, APP), describes itself as *"S_low is the delivered count — the **five-term return-on-capital series** surviving `robust_centre`"*, is *"Read against branch-d/v5-preregistration.md"*, and **keeps IDCC** (`IDCC 16 14 14 yes 11 yes`). - `probe_intangible_investment_intensity` V3.3 computes *"roic = robust centre of `NOPAT/IC` as filed"* and reports a cohort centre — *"top-quartile cut on rnd/capex over 12 issuers with a centre"*, *"vs centre 0.0205"* — with IDCC inside. No stance printed.

### QA-011
- **id:** QA-011
- **severity:** P1
- **status:** open
- **class:** product

**The §11 screen's boundary removes an issuer whose capital §11's argument does not reach: a patent licensor is dropped as if it were a bank.**

The screen is keyed on SIC `6000..=6799` — Division H, *Finance, Insurance, and Real Estate* — described in §11 as *"the Commission's boundary rather than ours."* Live output:

```
§11 class exclusion (SIC 6000..=6799, applied before any cohort statistic): removed 1 of 20 symbols [IDCC(SIC 6794)]
```

SIC **6794 is "Patent Owners and Lessors."** §11's economic argument is specific and does not extend to it: *"A bank's or insurer's balance sheet **is** its inventory: loans, deposits, float and reserves are the operating business"*, and *"interest income and expense **are** the operating business."* None of that describes a patent licensing company. §11's own class list is `FinancialServices` (banks, insurers) plus `NotEligible` (*"ETF, fund, crypto shell, REIT"*) — a patent licensor is neither.

The product's own measurement contradicts the exclusion: in `probe_option_one_survivor_count`, IDCC's five-term return-on-capital series resolves and survives (`14` kept high, `11` kept low, `dropped: 5 terms, 0 no-rate`) — a perfectly ordinary `equity + debt` issuer.

Direction of error is coverage loss, which the target specification explicitly guards against: `docs/roic-target-specification.md` row 14 warns that *"discarding usable evidence to make a target 'cleaner' is the coverage-shrinking move Decision 1 exists to prevent."*

Note the interaction with QA-010: IDCC is currently *retained* in `S` and in the ΔROIC centre and *removed* from the reinvestment centres. Fixing QA-010 by widening the screen without settling this boundary would propagate the wrong exclusion to more statistics, not fewer.

*suggested_fix:* complex — either narrow the SIC range to the sub-ranges §11's argument reaches (depository/insurance/holding, excluding 65xx real estate and 6794 patent lessors), or key the screen on the product's own `BusinessClass` and state why SIC was rejected. That is a fork, not a local edit; problem and evidence only.

My hypothesis was that a one-year autocorrelation is the wrong instrument — a durable firm-level advantage would show up as spread *between* firms, not within one. Testable from data already here:

So the fade isn't an artefact. It's the correct reading of evidence that contains no growth signal.

The model isn't wrong. It's **uninformed** — and the missing information has a specific shape: a growth signal that survives more than one year. Street pays 171x for VICR on a belief about the next decade that 251 observations of annual revenue growth can neither confirm nor refute.

**0.52x means: for a typical company, our model says it's worth about half of what the stock market says it's worth.**

That's it. If the market prices a company at $100 a share, our model comes out around $52.

Here's the concrete version, using two you know:

| | market price | what our model says |
|---|---|---|
| Microsoft | $500 | $261 |
| Apple | $313 | $105 |
| Amazon | $239 | $60 |

Half, a third, a quarter. Across the thirteen companies where the model produces a number at all, the middle one lands at 52% of the market price.

**Why that's a problem and not just "we found bargains":** if we thought *one* company was worth half its price, that's an interesting call — maybe the market is wrong about that one. But we're saying it about nearly all of them at once. When your model disagrees with the market about everything, the more likely explanation is that the model is missing something, not that the entire stock market is wrong.

That's exactly what you told me at the start — the numbers don't line up with the street, and that's what's wrong with our model.

**And the worse part I found today:** it's not that the model is uniformly too low. It's that the model gives almost every company the *same* answer. It can't tell a great business from an ordinary one. It thinks a small pharma company deserves a higher price than Apple. The market thinks Apple deserves three times more. So even if we ignored the "half" problem entirely and just used it to rank companies best-to-worst — which is what a screener is for — the ranking wouldn't be worth much.

**And the reason,** which is the useful part: the model tries to figure out whether a company's growth will last. It looked at twelve years of history for twenty companies and found it genuinely cannot tell — a fast-growing company this year is not reliably fast-growing next year, in the data we're feeding it. So the model does the honest thing and assumes growth fades away almost immediately. Once you assume that about everyone, everyone ends up worth roughly the same modest multiple.

So the model isn't broken. It's blind. It's being asked "is this company's growth durable?" and it's answering "I can't tell from what you've shown me" — and then pricing everything accordingly.

**TLDR** — 0.52x = our model values the typical company at about half its stock price (Microsoft $261 vs $500, Apple $105 vs $313). Worse, it gives nearly everyone the same answer, so it can't rank companies either. The cause: from the data we feed it, it can't detect whether any company's growth will last, so it assumes it won't — for everybody.

Fair challenge — and you're right. A single-scenario 10-year DCF is a teaching tool; nobody on a desk trades off one verbatim. But the honest answer isn't one secret replacement — it's that practitioners use three or four instruments, each fixing a specific DCF disease, and two of them map *directly* onto the residuals our scoreboard just exposed. Let me give you the real menu.

## What practitioners actually use

| method | in one sentence | what it fixes |
|---|---|---|
| **Residual income / economic profit** (RIM, "EVA", Holt CFROI) | Value = capital the company already has + the present value of profits *above* the cost of that capital | The terminal-value disease: most of the answer anchors in *measurable today* instead of a guess about year 10. Same theory as DCF, provably equivalent algebra — but with identical forecasts it empirically lands much closer to actual prices (this is well documented in the accounting literature) |
| **Reverse DCF / expectations investing** | Don't forecast to get a value — take the price and ask "what growth does this price *assume*?", then judge if that assumption is sane | Turns valuation from prediction into judgment. This is the single most-used fundamental tool at long/short shops |
| **Forward multiples, disciplined by a cross-cohort fit** | Value = consensus year-2 earnings × the multiple that companies with this growth/profitability *actually get* (one regression across the cohort, not per-name picks) | Matches how street targets are actually made (analysts literally publish "22× our 2027 EPS"). Finds *relative* cheapness |
| **ML return prediction** | Quant funds predict returns from hundreds of features | Not for us: it predicts returns, not values, it's unexplainable as a screener, and on 20 names it would just memorize the answers |

## Why this maps perfectly onto our residuals

- **AMZN at −97%, ORCL refused, MSFT −56%** — that's the DCF base disease: heavy investment torches this year's cash flow. In a residual-income model, capex stops being a penalty and becomes *capital that earns a measured return*. The NOPAT + ROIC machinery we already built on `roic-on` is literally the input set RIM needs. Our biggest residual and our already-built asset point at the same method.
- **WMT −64%, COST −57%** — the market pays a "quality premium" no 10-year fade can reach. Reverse DCF is the honest instrument there: report *what the price implies* (e.g., "WMT's price assumes ~X% growth for 15 years") and let the screener flag implausibility instead of pretending to know the true value.

## The one decision that's genuinely yours

The forward-multiple lane is the method most likely to hit ±5% — because it's calibrated on how the market prices fundamentals *across the cohort*. But that means prices enter the model as calibration input. Under rule v2 that's forbidden for our absolute-value lane — and there's a real economic consequence, not just a principle: a relative model **can never tell you the whole market is expensive**; it assumes the cohort is right on average and only finds outliers. Hedge funds accept that because they trade long *and* short. A discount screener might too — but that's a knowing trade-off, not a default.

## My recommendation

1. **v3 of the lab = switch the value engine from DCF to residual income**, keeping consensus estimates as inputs and the ladder discipline unchanged. Justification independent of street: it's the same theory re-anchored on measured capital, it kills the terminal-value dominance we've already diagnosed twice, and it's what our ROIC work was born for.
2. **Add a reverse-DCF column to the scoreboard** — "growth implied by the current price" next to "growth the street forecasts." Costs almost nothing, explains every residual.
3. **The relative-multiple lane only if you bless it** — as a separately-labeled *ranking* instrument, never mixed into the absolute value.

Say the word and v3 starts with the RIM engine; the relative lane waits for your explicit yes or no.

**TLDR** — Correct: nobody uses textbook DCF raw. The practitioner stack is: residual income models (anchor value in measured capital, not year-10 guesses — empirically lands closer to prices), reverse DCF (ask what the price implies instead of predicting), and forward multiples fitted cross-cohort (how street targets are actually made — but it needs prices as input, which only you can authorize under rule v2). Recommended: v3 = residual-income engine reusing our NOPAT/ROIC machinery + a reverse-DCF diagnostic column; relative lane pending your call.

Here is the proposal. I'll state it as a design, not code — nothing lands until you call it.

## The most ambitious street-blind engine I can defend: economic profit on *total* capital, with a measured competitive-advantage period

The deepest lesson of the ladder so far: every disease we've killed was a place where the model's *capital base* or *duration* was wrong, not its arithmetic. ABBV's negative book, AAPL's $4/share book, HD's +1409% ROE, MA at 178% — all one disease (book equity is not the capital the business runs on). And the open terminal fork is a duration question the current engine cannot answer, only choose. The ambitious engine fixes both structurally, and the fork dissolves rather than getting decided.

**Engine.** Enterprise economic profit: `value = invested capital + Σ PV(NOPAT_t − WACC·IC_{t−1}) − net debt`, per share. Same residual-income mathematics we already trust, moved to the enterprise side where the capital base is measurable for every issuer — including ABBV, which becomes valuable again instead of refused.

**Total capital, not book capital.** Invested capital = operating capital **+ capitalized R&D + capitalized organizational capital** (Peters–Taylor 2017: R&D by perpetual inventory at a literature amortization rate, ~30% of SG&A as organizational capital). For this cohort that's the difference between "NVDA earns 140% on capital" (meaningless, decays instantly in any fade model) and "NVDA earns ~40% on the capital it actually deploys, including a decade of expensed R&D" (a measurable franchise with measurable decay). This is what makes fade dynamics *mean something*.

**Growth is paid for, structurally.** Reinvestment is tied to growth by the identity `g = b × ROIIC` (the repo already codifies this in `evidence_sotp.rs`): each projected year's growth consumes capital at the *measured incremental* capital intensity. The v4a/v4b caps stop being caps and become a **coherence check**: if consensus growth implies reinvestment the filed history says the issuer has never achieved, that's a named flag, not a silent haircut.

**The terminal fork dissolves.** Instead of fading *growth* to 2.5% and then arguing about ω, fade **ROIC toward WACC** over a competitive-advantage period (CAP), the HOLT/CFROI structure. At the fade's end, economic profit is zero by construction — the terminal is just invested capital compounding at WACC, worth exactly PV(IC). No Gordon denominator, no ω dial, no terminal-growth dial. The *only* economic lever is CAP length, and CAP is **measured**: excess-ROIC persistence per issuer, shrunk toward the cohort estimate by empirical Bayes (the honest answer to 3–5 filed years per firm — our probe showed the cross-section clears the noise floor 31.7×, so the shrinkage target is real signal). Cross-sectional shrinkage is also the statistical backbone: the cohort is valued jointly, not one-at-a-time.

**Output is a distribution, not a point.** The consensus tables carry low/high/analyst-count per estimate — measured forward uncertainty, street-blind (they're fundamentals forecasts). Propagate them: each name gets a central value **and an interval**. The scoreboard gains a falsifiable instrument: does street's target fall inside our measured interval, and is the interval honest (too-narrow = overconfident, too-wide = uninformative)? Phase 2 small caps will have wide intervals — that's the model being honest, visibly.

## All inputs

**Consensus (forward — allowed under rule v2):**

| # | input | source |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | EPS 0y/+1y: avg, low, high, analyst count, year-ago | yfinance `earnings_estimate` |
| 2 | Revenue 0y/+1y: same fields | `revenue_estimate` |
| 3 | LTG where published (mostly absent — refusal-safe) | `growth_estimates` |

**Filed history (10–15y, SEC EDGAR companyfacts — the Rust side's `edgar.rs` + curated qname policy in `shared/contracts/sec-driver-normalization.json` already exist; Python hits the same free API and inherits the curation):**

| # | input | used for |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | revenue | growth durability, through-cycle margin |
| 5 | pretax income, interest expense, tax rate | NOPAT (the wave-1 fix — interest paid ≠ interest expense — carries over) |
| 6 | total debt, stockholders' equity incl. NCI, cash | invested capital, net debt |
| 7 | R&D expense series | intangible capital (perpetual inventory) |
| 8 | SG&A series | organizational capital |
| 9 | capex, depreciation | capital intensity, ROIIC |
| 10 | share count series | drift (v4b survives), per-share conversion |
| 11 | dividends, buybacks | payout/distribution policy |
| 12 | goodwill | organic vs acquired capital split (optional tier) |
| 13 | segment revenue | SOTP tier (optional, later) |

**Policy constants (a-priori, global, ledgered):**

| # | input | note |
|---|---|---|
| 14 | risk-free rate | fetched actual 10y Treasury, not hardcoded |
| 15 | ERP 4.5% + Blume beta | as now; leverage-adjusting beta needs market D/E = **price leak — rejected** |
| 16 | long-run nominal growth anchor (~4% GDP) | fade destination for *revenue*; excess returns die by CAP, not by this |
| 17 | R&D amortization rate, SG&A capitalization fraction | literature (Peters–Taylor); one global value each, no industry branches |

**Derived measurements (no dials):** ROIC on total capital, incremental ROIC, excess-ROIC persistence → CAP with cohort shrinkage, through-cycle margin, reinvestment coherence vs consensus.

## What I'd explicitly keep out

Market prices in any input (relative lane stays gated on your yes); ML/black-box components (untunable without street leakage, unfalsifiable when wrong); macro scenarios. And two honest flags: this is a big complexity step (KISS says we ladder into it — capital base first, then CAP fade, then distributions, each an isolated rung with its own ledger entry), and EDGAR fetching in Python is real work — though it converges the prototype onto the extraction machinery the Rust port already owns, which makes the eventual port a translation instead of a rewrite.

**TLDR:** Most ambitious defensible engine: enterprise economic profit on **total capital** (R&D + organizational capital capitalized), growth paid for via `g = b × ROIIC`, excess returns fading to zero over a **measured** competitive-advantage period (empirical-Bayes shrinkage across the cohort) — which dissolves the terminal fork instead of deciding it — and a value **distribution** per name from consensus dispersion. Inputs: 3 consensus tables, ~10 EDGAR filed series (reusing the repo's curated qname policy), 4 a-priori constants, zero dials. If you bless it, I'd ladder in: capital base → CAP fade → distributions, one rung at a time.

Me parece dos cosas a la vez, y vale la pena separarlas con honestidad: como **estrella polar** es excelente — y converge con partes de lo que ya decidimos — pero como **próximo paso de construcción** violaría las tres reglas que nos mantienen honestos, y casi todo el documento es inconstruible con la evidencia que existe. Dejame defender ambas mitades.

## Dónde converge con lo que ya tenemos

Tres de sus ideas centrales son exactamente el v6 que te propuse, con otro vocabulario: **#14** (growth no es input, emerge de `reinvestment × ROIIC`) es el `g = b × ROIIC` de mi propuesta; **#46** (terminal endógeno: simular hasta que el economic profit → 0) es literalmente el CAP fade que disuelve el fork del terminal; **#7/#8** (claims tipados + provenance) es la cultura que el ledger ya practica — refusals con nombre, justificación antes del scoreboard, decomposición de Rung 0. Y **#31** (nunca votación de agentes; la decisión deriva del modelo formal) ya es ley acá. Eso me da confianza en la dirección económica compartida.

## El problema central: expresividad sin identificabilidad

El documento optimiza para que el modelo pueda *representar* todo. Nuestra restricción vinculante es otra: que cada parámetro pueda ser **medido desde evidencia o fijado a priori** — nunca autorado por analista, nunca por-empresa, nunca ajustado a street.

El dato duro de esta semana: con 3 años de historia archivada **no pudimos identificar un solo parámetro** (ω = 0.76 ± 0.24 — el intervalo contiene tanto 0.62 como 1.0). El digital twin de **#1** necesita miles de parámetros latentes *por empresa*: willingness to pay, switching costs, respuestas estratégicas de competidores, incentivos de management. Ninguno tiene serie observable. Cada uno terminaría siendo el juicio de alguien vestido de matemática — la misma enfermedad de "número fabricado" que el ledger mata cada dos commits, pero a escala industrial. Y un modelo que puede justificar cualquier valor no verifica nada: es una máquina de racionalización, no de valuación. El modelo más ambicioso no es el que representa todo; es **el más ambicioso que todavía puede ser refutado por los datos**.

Además los twins por-empresa con estructura causal por-empresa rompen "una receta global, cero tuning por nombre" — y vos mismo nombraste por qué esa regla existe: con parámetros latentes por nombre, aterrizar cerca de street es una tautología.

## Los conflictos directos con la regla v2

**#12** (buybacks condicionados a `stock_price/intrinsic_value`), **#23** (narrative engine), **#24-25** (market-pricing engine, catalysts), **#26** (reflexivity) — todos consumen precio de mercado. El propio documento dice "nunca mezclarlos": esa separación es exactamente nuestra lane relativa, que está gateada a tu sí explícito. Como lane *separada*, algún día, bien; dentro del intrinsic engine, nunca.

Y un detalle que me gusta señalar porque el documento se refuta elegantemente a sí mismo: **#32 (Value of Information) es el criterio para podar el propio documento.** El tax engine de #40, el supply-chain graph de #19, el regime engine de #22 — para nuestro cohort, VOI casi seguro dice "$1/share, no investigar". El documento propone 50 componentes y también propone la herramienta que demuestra que ~40 no valen su costo todavía.

## Lo que me robaría ya mismo (street-blind, medible, barato)

1. **Falsifiers en el ledger** (#6): cada entrada de cambio gana una línea `falsified_if:`. Costo cero, formaliza lo que ya hacemos.
2. **Claims tipados** (#7): etiquetar cada input de la receta como FACT (archivado) / FORECAST (consenso) / POLICY (constante a priori) / MEASURED (derivado). Una columna más en la tabla de receta.
3. **VOI** (#32-33): en cuanto aterricen las distribuciones del v6, `∂value/∂input × incertidumbre(input)` es computable y street-blind — y se convierte en el **router** que decide qué componente del world model se construye después, por valor medido y no por elegancia. Es la mejor idea construible de todo el documento.
4. **Adding-up constraint** (#10): sumar los revenue forecasts de consenso de una industria contra el crecimiento del mercado — como *instrumento de coherencia* del scoreboard, no como input. Detecta el error clásico del consenso.
5. Más adelante, como rungs medidos: **#42** (dilución simulada desde SBC/options archivados — mejora real sobre share count) y **#47** (mortalidad como hazard de cohort con base rates históricos).

## Mi recomendación de secuencia

No cambia: **v5 capital base total → CAP fade (que ya es el #46) → distribuciones**. Ahí el sistema gana VOI, y VOI decide con números qué pieza del world model justifica existir. El world model sin un core de valuación validado es una catedral sobre arena — y notá que el documento no tiene scoreboard: su loop de aprendizaje (#27) se cierra recién cuando los forecasts realizan, o sea *años*. Nuestro scoreboard cierra en 90 segundos. Esa asimetría es la razón por la que la escalera existe.

**TLDR:** Como visión a largo plazo: sí, y converge con v6 en lo económico (`g = b·ROIIC`, terminal endógeno, claims tipados). Como próximo build: no — sus piezas centrales son no-identificables (miles de parámetros latentes cuando no pudimos fijar uno), varias consumen precio (viola regla v2), y los twins por-empresa rompen la receta global. Me robo ya: falsifiers en el ledger, claims tipados, adding-up check, y VOI — que además es el criterio que poda el propio documento. Secuencia igual: capital base → CAP → distribuciones, y de ahí VOI decide qué parte del world model se gana el derecho a existir.
